steps.message:
Item 051 on the Package A verification register is assigned to me and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the Level-3 placement. It covers the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them.

Work through Item 051 against the project record and issue the verification memo. Set out what you reviewed, the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition. Where something has to be produced before the item can be closed, say what it is and who is required to produce it.

Use the attached memorandum form and keep its sections. Write it from Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer, to Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, copied to Rachel Marlbeck. Save it as Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx.

["One-dimensional incremental-load consolidation testing was performed in accordance with ASTM D2435, Method A (24-hour load-increment duration; load-increment ratio LIR = 1.0; back-pressure saturation confirmed with B-value ≥ 0.96 on each specimen). Fixed-ring floating consolidometer, initial specimen diameter 63.5 mm, initial specimen height 25.4 mm. Deformation-time readings recorded at 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 30, 60, 120, 240, 480, and 1,440 minutes. Coefficient of consolidation c_v computed by Taylor's √t method at each increment.  1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
 Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
 a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
 Block B.
 The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
 approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
 footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
 approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
 The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
      • Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
      existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
      • Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
      normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
      permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
      between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
      • Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
      pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
 Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
      • The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
      shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
      groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
      • A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
      through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
      confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
 Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
 B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
 an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
 σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
 stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
 (Cr) compression.
 Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
       1. Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
       compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
       by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
       settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
       2. Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
       within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
       must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
       elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

       hydrostatic head.
       3. Block B piles — Because of anticipated fill-induced consolidation of the underlying clay and the
       resulting downdrag loads, and because column loads at Block B exceed the safe capacity of shallow
       foundations bearing on the upper sand, closed-end driven pipe piles carried through the upper sand and the
       clay to bearing in the dense sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0 are recommended. The pile design
       must address soil-pile interaction from clay consolidation, as the engineered fill load induces downdrag on
       piles driven through the consolidating clay (Section 8.3).
       4. Block B plant-room excavation — The plant-room subgrade is planned near El. 726.0, i.e., inside the
       clay aquitard, approximately 6 ft above the top of the confined aquifer at El. 720.0. Because the confined
       piezometric head (El. 738.0) is approximately 12 ft above the planned subgrade elevation, this excavation
       will develop a significant uplift pressure on the clay plug from the underlying aquifer.
       The base-heave stability of the plug must be evaluated by the design team, and pressure-relief
       or aquifer-drawdown measures may be required. This condition is called out as the controlling
       constructability issue for the plant-room excavation and must be addressed by the Contractor’s dewatering
       and shoring designs.
       5. Engineered fill over the clay — The 12 ft of engineered fill required beneath Block B (from El. 738.0
       up to El. 750.0) will constitute a net surcharge on the normally-consolidated compressible clay across the
       Block B footprint. Because σ'p ≈ σ'0, the entire increment is virgin compression under Cc. The Owner is
       advised that consolidation of the underlying clay under this fill surcharge will occur, that the associated
       settlement will affect the behavior of any deep foundations driven from the raised working grade before
       the consolidation is substantially complete, and that these effects must be considered in the pile design.

 Authorization for the geotechnical investigation was issued by Thornbury State University, Office of Capital
 Programs, under Kelbrook Geotechnical Proposal P-2024-116 dated September 6, 2024, and Notice-to-Proceed

 2.2 Project Description
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program consists of three student-housing blocks:
      • Block A — six-story residential tower over a shared podium, seated on a basement mat foundation.
      • Block B — six-story residential tower over a shared podium, seated on the same basement mat
      foundation as Block A, with a separate deep plant-room excavation planned in the southwest quadrant of
      the block footprint (elevator and mechanical/electrical service space, approximately 24 ft below design
      grade).
      • Block C — six-story residential tower over the shared podium, on spread footings; no basement is
      planned beneath Block C.

 The shared podium is a one-story reinforced-concrete transfer structure below the residential towers. Finished

 2. Excavation Observations — Block A Basement
 2.1 Excavation Opening and Progression




Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A                                             Page 1
 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.                                                                                     Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528




 The Block A basement excavation was opened in the northeast quadrant of the Package A footprint on

 lean-concrete working mat). The excavation was carried out by the Contractor using a mid-size hydraulic
 excavator with side dumping to trucks; sequence proceeded from the east perimeter westward across the Block
 A footprint over the course of approximately three weeks.
 Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
 open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
 Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
 dated 06/04/2025, was activated on 07/12/2025, two days before the first cut, and remained in operation
 continuously through mat placement on 01/12/2026 and thereafter to protect the wall pour sequence.

 2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
 Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
 Section 6 of the reference report:
   •    From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
        root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
        downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
        structural fill re-use.
   •    From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
        the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
        Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
        dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.
   •    From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
        a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent
        within ± 0.5 ft across the Block A footprint. The clay retained a vertical or near-vertical face for the
        excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)
        produced no rutting or pumping under the loaded haul truck used for the check.
 The transition from Stratum 1 (upper sand) to Stratum 2 (clay) at El. 738.0 was sharp and well-defined in the cut
 face and matched the elevation logged in Borings B-01, B-02, B-07 and B-09 within a few tenths of a foot.

 Subgrade at El. 730.0 was inspected on 08/06/2025 in the presence of the Contractor’s Superintendent (Mr.

 installation was recorded in the deep-aquifer piezometers.

                                       SECTION 31 20 00

PART 1    GENERAL

   1.1 SUMMARY
   A. Section Includes:
         1. Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
            pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
         2.    Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
              building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
         3. Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
         4. Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
   B. Related Sections:
         1.    Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
              envelope.
         2. Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
         3. Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
            subgrade.

   1.2 REFERENCES
   A.    Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
         cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
         1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
              only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
         2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
              Package A structural fill.
         3. ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
            and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
            method.
         4.     ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
              (Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content




                                         31 20 00 - Page 1 of 6
                                             Earth Moving
           when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
     5. ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
        Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
        Engineer of Record.

1.3 DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
     beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
     meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B. Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.    Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
     maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.    Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
     content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.    Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
     whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
     by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.

1.4 QUALITY ASSURANCE
A. Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
   Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
   directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
   lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.    Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
     documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
     shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
     the start of each testing day.
C.     Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
     moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
     determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
     the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
     D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
     accepted.

1.5 SUBMITTALS
A. Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
     1.    Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
          Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
     2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
          D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
     3.    Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
          passes.
B. During placement, submit daily:




                                     31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
          1. Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
            density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
            and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
            deviation from optimum.

   1.6 SEQUENCING
   A.     No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
         presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
   B.     No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
         accepted per Article 3.4.

PART 2    PRODUCTS

   2.1 STRUCTURAL FILL
   A.     Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
         D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
   B.     Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
         the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
   C.     Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
         particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
   D.    Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
         shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
         Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
         which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.

   2.2 COMMON FILL
   A. Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
      frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.

   2.3 CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
   A. Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
      placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.

PART 3    EXECUTION

   3.1 EXAMINATION
   A.     Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
         that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
         Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.

   3.2 SUBGRADE PREPARATION
   A. Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
      structural fill.
   B. Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
      approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present




                                          31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
                                              Earth Moving
      to witness the proof roll.
C.    Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
     Section.

3.3 PLACEMENT
A. Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.    Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
     the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.    Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
     requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.     Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
     precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
     3.4.B.

3.4 COMPACTION
A. Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
   Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
   moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
   (self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
   structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
   within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
   Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
   Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
   placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
   intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
   general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
   compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
   compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
   shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B. Acceptance Criteria.
             Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
             95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
             placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
             of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
             be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
             D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
             5,000 sf per lift.

C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
     not satisfied at any test location:
     1.    The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
          recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
     2.    Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
          criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.




                                     31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
      3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
          compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.    Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
     location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
     density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
     test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
     density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.

3.5 BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A. Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
   specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
   place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.    Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
     thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C. Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
   structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.

3.6 SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
     0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.    Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
     constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
     predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
     Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
     written disposition is issued.
C.    Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
     be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
     Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
     immediately.

3.7 FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A. Testing frequency for structural fill:
     1. In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
        Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
     2.    Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
          Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
          change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.    Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
     report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
     dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
     density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
     optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.    Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
     D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
     placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.



                                      31 20 00 - Page 5 of 6
                                          Earth Moving
       3.8 PROTECTION
      A.     Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
           precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.
           Rework and retest, at the Contractor's expense, any area disturbed or softened prior to
           permanent cover.

exit_code=0
3.  BASIS OF REVIEW

Governing tolerance.  Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.6 (“Settlement Tolerance”) establishes the controlling criteria: total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement 0.5 in maximum over 30 ft. Article 3.6 further provides that “where predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a written disposition is issued,” and that cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance is to be reported immediately.

Design basis.  Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001 Rev.2, Section 7.3, states that Block C is founded on isolated spread footings bearing on the upper sand above the compressible CL clay, that “settlement of the clay layer is a serviceability consideration and is checked in CB-GEO-007,” and that settlement is checked under service-level combinations with tolerances established in Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 (total 1.0 in, differential 0.5 in). The DBM lists the governing clay parameters (H = 18 ft; γ = 120 pcf; Cc = 0.28; e0 = 0.92; σ’0 = 1,850 psf; σ’p = 1,900 psf) and the Block C allowable bearing pressure of 4,000 psf net (at El. 748 ± 2 ft).

Geotechnical basis.  GIR Rev.2, Executive Summary (recommendation 1) and Sections 8.1 and 9.1, assigns the consolidation-settlement computation to the Structural Engineer of Record: the EOR “must explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress increase q at mid-depth of the clay caused by each governing footing, using the parameters in Table 5-1,” and “must reconcile [it] against the total-and-differential settlement tolerances.” Section 8.1 gives the one-dimensional consolidation equation and Table 8-1 a sensitivity table of Sc against q. Section 9.1 states that if computed settlement exceeds tolerance, “footing sizes may be adjusted to reduce the stress increase, footings may be combined into a mat, or a deep-foundation alternative may be considered.”

Parameters applied.  The consolidation parameters are taken from Vantree report VMT-2025-0109-CON (ASTM D2435, samples B-06 U3 and B-08 U2), as transcribed in GIR Table 5-1 and CB-GEO-007 Sheet 5, and as recorded on the Register Reference Values tab: Cc = 0.28; Cr = 0.045; e0 = 0.92; σ’0 = 1,850 psf (mid-clay, El. 729.0); σ’p = 1,900 psf (OCR 1.03, essentially normally consolidated); H = 18 ft (El. 738.0 to El. 720.0); double drainage; cv ≈ 0.042 ft²/day. The stress increase at mid-clay, Δσ = 900 psf, is as recorded in CB-GEO-007 (Sheet 2 and Sheet 5) and on the Register Reference Values tab.

Basis of review applied.  I (a) confirmed whether CB-GEO-007 contains a complete long-term (consolidation) settlement analysis; (b) independently computed the one-dimensional consolidation settlement of the Stratum 2 clay using the GIR §8.1 equation and the recorded parameters and Δσ; (c) compared the result to the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 tolerances; (d) checked the founding geometry used in the calculation against the issued-for-construction drawings; and (e) correlated the result with the Block C monitoring record and its trend.



4.  FINDINGS

Finding 1 — The settlement calculation of record does not contain a long-term (consolidation) analysis.  CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4, titled “Consolidation — Long-Term Settlement Contribution — Stratum 2 CL Clay,” is left incomplete: every parameter cell carries “—” and the sheet states “Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3” (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 4).

The calculation’s serviceability conclusion rests solely on the immediate (elastic) settlement computed on Sheet 3 by the Schmertmann strain-influence method — maximum total 0.9 in (footing F-C6) and maximum differential 0.2 in — both reported within the 1.0 in / 0.5 in tolerance (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 3, “Conclusion (Sheet 3)” and “Comparison to Tolerance”).

That computation is explicitly short-term: the time factor C2 is set to 1.00 with t = 0.1 yr, and the Stratum 2 modulus used is a back-figured undrained Eu (≈ 150 tsf). It is an immediate-settlement computation, not a long-term settlement computation (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 3, correction factors and soil-modulus table).

Item 051 is expressly the long-term settlement of the clay. The DBM (§7.3) states that the clay settlement is “checked in CB-GEO-007,” and the drawing note on Detail 3/S-201 states “Refer to CB-GEO-007 for settlement calculation basis.” The long-term component is therefore required but absent (DBM Rev.2, §7.3; Sheet S-201, Detail 3/S-201, Notes).

The settlement analysis in CB-GEO-007 is incomplete for the purpose of Item 051.

Finding 2 — The Geotechnical Investigation Report assigns the consolidation computation to the EOR and supplies the method and a sensitivity table.  GIR Rev.2 (Executive Summary, recommendation 1; §9.1) provides that Block C spread footings may be founded in the upper sand, but requires that “the Structural Engineer of Record must explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress increase q at mid-depth of the clay caused by each governing footing, using the parameters in Table 5-1,” and that “the computed settlement must be reconciled against the total-and-differential settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.”

GIR §8.1 states the one-dimensional consolidation equation, Sc = Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[(σ’0 + q) / σ’0], and that for any q > (σ’p − σ’0) ≈ 50 psf, virgin (Cc) compression governs (GIR Rev.2, §8.1).

GIR Table 8-1 tabulates the sensitivity of Sc to q at mid-clay: q = 100 psf → 0.7 in; 300 → 2.1 in; 600 → 3.8 in; 1,000 → 5.9 in; 1,200 → 6.8 in (GIR Rev.2, Table 8-1).

Finding 3 — Independent consolidation computation using the recorded Δσ = 900 psf exceeds the total-settlement tolerance by a factor of about five.  Working — applying the GIR §8.1 equation with the recorded parameters (Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, H = 18 ft = 216 in, σ’0 = 1,850 psf) and the recorded stress increase at mid-clay Δσ = 900 psf (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 2 and Sheet 5; Register, Reference Values):

Sc = [Cc · H / (1 + e0)] · log10[(σ’0 + Δσ) / σ’0]

   = [0.28 × 216 / (1 + 0.92)] · log10[(1,850 + 900) / 1,850]

   = [60.48 / 1.92] · log10[2,750 / 1,850]

   = 31.50 × log10[1.4865]

   = 31.50 × 0.17228

   ≈ 5.42 in.

A recompression/virgin split — Cr from σ’0 to σ’p, then Cc from σ’p to (σ’0 + Δσ) — gives Sc ≈ 0.06 in + 5.06 in = 5.12 in, essentially the same result, because the OCR is only 1.03 and nearly the full 900 psf increment lies on the virgin branch (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 5; GIR Table 5-1).

The result is consistent with GIR Table 8-1: it falls between the q = 600 psf (3.8 in) and q = 1,000 psf (5.9 in) entries, as 900 psf does. I verified the Table 8-1 entries by recomputation (q = 100 → 0.72 in; 300 → 2.06 in; 600 → 3.84 in; 1,000 → 5.91 in; 1,200 → 6.84 in).

Comparison to tolerance: Sc ≈ 5.42 in against the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 total limit of 1.0 in is a utilisation of about 5.4×. Adding the immediate settlement (0.9 in, Schmertmann) gives a long-term total of about 6.3 in, about 6× the tolerance. The long-term settlement exceeds the total-settlement tolerance by a wide margin.

The result does not turn on the precise value of Δσ. Back-solving the GIR equation, the consolidation settlement reaches 1.0 in at q ≈ 140 psf and 0.5 in at q ≈ 70 psf. Any realistic spread-footing stress increase at this site produces a q at mid-clay well above 140 psf, so the total-settlement tolerance is exceeded for any plausible footing-induced stress.

Finding 4 — The founding elevation used in CB-GEO-007 does not match the issued-for-construction drawings and must be reconciled.  CB-GEO-007, Sheet 2, takes the underside of footing at El. 740.5, described as “isolated square spread footings on Stratum 1 sand, ~2.5 ft above top of clay” (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 2).

The issued drawings show the Block C typical spread footing with top of footing at El. 748.0 and underside at El. 746.0 (2’-0” thick), i.e., about 8 ft above the top of the Stratum 2 clay at El. 738.0. The DBM states the 4,000 psf allowable bearing is applicable “at El. 748 ± 2 ft,” consistent with the drawings (Sheet S-201, Detail 3/S-201; DBM Rev.2, geotechnical parameters). Boring B-09 (Block C centre) logs the SP-SM upper sand from about El. 746.1 to the clay contact at El. 738.0, confirming that the El. 746.0 founding lies within the upper sand (Boring Logs, B-09).

The monitored column pedestals, at top elevations about El. 750.05, are consistent with a roughly 2 ft pedestal on a footing topped at El. 748.0 (the drawing geometry), not with a footing topped at about El. 743 (the calc geometry), corroborating the drawing founding (Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 2 — Monitoring Points).

Consequence: the Δσ = 900 psf recorded in CB-GEO-007 was computed for a founding 5.5 ft deeper (closer to the clay) than the issued drawings, and so over-states the stress at mid-clay relative to the as-drawn/as-built geometry. A founding at El. 746.0 would reduce Δσ, and the EOR must recompute Δσ at mid-clay for the as-drawn footing schedule (Sheet S-101) and founding. This is a reconciliation item. It does not change Finding 3 in substance: even a substantially reduced Δσ yields a consolidation settlement well above the 1.0 in tolerance (GIR Table 8-1: q = 300 psf → 2.1 in; q = 600 psf → 3.8 in).

Finding 5 — The settlement monitoring is consistent with the early stage of a large, slow consolidation and does not support closure against the tolerance.  The latest reading, 06/26/2026, is 0.61 in cumulative at MP-7 (interior footing FTG-C7, heaviest tributary load), with the twelve points ranging from 0.31 in (MP-12) to 0.61 in (MP-7). All values are within the 1.0 in total tolerance to date (Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 3 — Readings, Round 15; Sheet 1 — Observations Summary).

The trend has not stabilised. The round-to-round increment at MP-7 has risen from 0.03 in per 14 days (Rounds 2–4) to 0.07 in per 14 days (Round 14–15). The record states that “the incremental settlement observed in the most recent three rounds … is equal to or greater than the incremental settlement observed in the first three rounds” and “Rate not decreasing.” The trend chart annotation records the curve as concave (downward) and that it “has not entered a decelerating (concave-up) phase” (Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 1 — Observations Summary; Sheet 4 — Trend Chart; Sheet 3 — Round-to-Round Increment at Worst Point).

The structure is still being loaded. The monitoring log records: footings and pedestals cast 12/2025; Level-1 columns and Level-2 slab framing 01–02/2026; Level-2 CMU partitions, Level-3 framing and roof steel 03–05/2026; podium slab-on-grade placed 06/2026. Full service (dead plus live) load is not yet applied (Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 5 — Notes).

Time-rate. With cv ≈ 0.042 ft²/day and double drainage (drainage path Hdr = 9 ft), primary consolidation is slow: about 90% consolidation in roughly 1,635 days (≈ 4.5 years), consistent with the GIR §8.1 statement that primary consolidation “require[s] on the order of several years.” At 196 days of monitoring, the average degree of consolidation is on the order of one-third, and less in practice because load is applied progressively (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 5; GIR Rev.2, §8.1).

Correlation. The 0.61 in observed is small relative to the computed ≈ 5.4 in ultimate consolidation and is consistent with a partially loaded structure in the early stage of a multi-year consolidation. The accelerating, non-decaying trend is the expected signature of that condition. The monitoring therefore corroborates, rather than refutes, the concern that the long-term settlement will exceed the tolerance; it is not a basis on which Item 051 can be closed against the tolerance.



5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION

Determination.  The Block C settlement analysis of record (CB-GEO-007) is not complete for the purpose of Item 051: it computes the immediate (elastic) settlement only and omits the long-term consolidation settlement of the Stratum 2 CL clay, which the GIR (§8.1, §9.1) and the DBM (§7.3) require the EOR to compute and reconcile against the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 tolerances. My independent computation of that long-term settlement, using the project’s own recorded parameters and Δσ = 900 psf, gives Sc ≈ 5.4 in — about 5.4 times the 1.0 in total-settlement tolerance (and about 6.3 in combined with the 0.9 in immediate settlement). The result exceeds the total-settlement tolerance for any realistic stress increase at this site, and the Block C monitoring (0.61 in, accelerating, non-decaying, structure not yet fully loaded, multi-year consolidation) is consistent with the early stage of that settlement.

Disposition.  NOT VERIFIED. Item 051 cannot be closed on the present record. I recommend the register item be held Open, with the Thelbridge disposition recorded as NOT VERIFIED (design review), pending the EOR action set out below.

Action required before the item can be closed.

1.  The Structural Engineer of Record — Gregory Nash, PE, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC — must complete and reissue the Block C settlement calculation (CB-GEO-007, Rev. X) to include the long-term one-dimensional consolidation settlement of the Stratum 2 CL clay, computed per the GIR §8.1 equation with the Table 5-1 parameters, for the as-drawn/as-built footing geometry. The reissue must in particular:

a.  Reconcile the founding elevation — the calculation is to use the issued-drawing founding (underside of footing El. 746.0 per Sheet S-201, Detail 3/S-201, within the DBM El. 748 ± 2 ft bearing band), not El. 740.5.

b.  Recompute the per-footing stress increase at mid-clay (El. 729.0) by Boussinesq/Newmark superposition for the as-drawn footing schedule (Sheet S-101) and founding.

c.  Compute the consolidation settlement (recompression plus virgin, recognising OCR 1.03) for each governing footing and add the immediate (Schmertmann) settlement, to give the total long-term settlement.

d.  Compute the differential settlement between adjacent footings and check it against the 0.5 in-over-30 ft limit.

e.  Reconcile the result explicitly against Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 (1.0 in total / 0.5 in differential).

2.  Because the predicted long-term settlement exceeds the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 tolerance, the EOR must issue a written disposition of the Block C foundation scheme. The remedies identified in GIR §9.1 are available to the EOR: enlarge or combine footings to reduce the stress increase, convert to a mat foundation, or adopt a deep-foundation alternative. The EOR’s written disposition is a required deliverable.

3.  Until the EOR’s written disposition is issued, and in accordance with Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6, no additional load is to be applied to the Block C foundations. I recommend that the Owner’s Representative (Adrian Vance) notify the Structural Engineer of Record in writing of the predicted exceedance, transmitting this verification, so that the Article 3.6 process is formally initiated and the load restriction is placed on the record.

4.  Block C settlement monitoring (Rowan Bay Constructors, Survey Crew 3 — D. Halloran, PLS) is to continue at the established 14-day interval, or as the EOR directs following the disposition, with readings transmitted to the Owner’s Representative; cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance is to be reported immediately per Article 3.6. Monitoring is an observation of performance; it is not, by itself, a closure deliverable for this item.

Deliverables required to close Item 051, and by whom.

•  Revised Block C settlement calculation (CB-GEO-007, Rev. X) including the long-term consolidation settlement, reconciled to Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 — to be produced by Gregory Nash, PE, Structural Engineer of Record, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC.

•  Written disposition of the Block C foundation scheme (response to the predicted exceedance) — to be produced by the same (EOR).

•  Written notification to the EOR of the predicted exceedance and the Article 3.6 load restriction, on Thelbridge letterhead — to be issued by Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, Thelbridge Project Management Services.

•  Continued settlement monitoring and transmission — to be produced by Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc. (Survey Crew 3); to be reviewed by the Geotechnical Reviewer.

Once the EOR’s revised calculation and written disposition are received and verified by the Geotechnical Reviewer, Item 051 may be re-evaluated for closure.

================ PAGE 1 ================
THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES
500 South High Street, Suite 720, Columbus, OH 43215 | (614) 555-0125 | thelbridgepm.com


VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM
To:         Adrian Vance — Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Owner’s
Representative, Thelbridge Project Management Services
From:             Rahul Nimkar — Geotechnical Reviewer, Thelbridge Project Management
Services
Date:             07/20/2026
Subject:          Verification of Register Item 051 — Block C Spread-Footing Long-Term
Settlement over the CL Clay Aquitard (Package A)
Cc:               Rachel Marlbeck — University Program Director, Thornbury State
University, Office of Capital Programs (Owner)


1. PURPOSE
This memorandum addresses Verification Register Item 051 of the Thelbridge Review
Comment and Verification Register — Package A. The item was raised by the Geotechnical
Reviewer on 07/10/2026, is assigned to the Geotechnical Reviewer (Rahul Nimkar), and is
required to be closed in signed form by 07/20/2026, two days ahead of the 07/22/2026 Level-3
concrete placement hold-point.
Item 051 requires verification of the Block C spread-footing foundations for long-term
settlement over the compressible CL clay aquitard (Stratum 2; Cc 0.28, e0 0.92, σ’p 1,900 psf;
18 ft layer), with a recorded stress increase at mid-layer of Δσ 900 psf, against the project
settlement tolerance of 1.0 in total and 0.5 in differential. The item further requires
confirmation that the settlement analysis is complete and reconciled against those tolerances,
and correlation with the Block C settlement-monitoring reading of 0.61 in cumulative recorded
on 06/26/2026.
The determinations sought by this memorandum are: (a) whether the Block C settlement
analysis of record (Calculation CB-GEO-007) is complete for the long-term settlement
condition; and (b) whether the long-term settlement of the Stratum 2 clay, so computed, lies
within the project tolerances.


2. DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
Primary reference documents listed for Item 051:
1. Geotechnical Investigation Report, KGI-2024-0417, Rev.2, Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.,
dated 02/14/2025 (“GIR Rev.2”).
2. Laboratory Consolidation Test Report VMT-2025-0109-CON, ASTM D2435, Vantree
Materials Testing, LLC, dated 01/09/2025 (file Consolidation_Test_Data_D2435.xlsx).
3. Calculation CB-GEO-007, “Block C Spread Footing Settlement,” Rev.0, Calloway Braddock
Structural Engineers, LLC, dated 09/30/2025 (file CB-GEO-007_Settlement_BlockC.xlsx).
4. Thelbridge Review Comment and Verification Register — Package A (file
Thelbridge_Verification_Register_PkgA.xlsx), last updated 07/15/2026 — Register entry Item
051 and the Reference Values tab.
5. Specification Section 31 20 00, “Earth Moving,” Rev.3, Calloway Braddock, dated
03/06/2026 — Article 3.6, Settlement Tolerance.
6. Settlement Monitoring Records — Block C (file SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14.xlsx), Rowan Bay
Constructors, Inc., Survey Crew 3, latest reading 06/26/2026.
7. Geotechnical Index Test Data, Vantree Materials Testing, LLC, report dated 01/09/2025
(file Geotech_Index_Test_Data.xlsx; lab project VMT-2024-0917-PkgA-INDEX).
 ================ PAGE 2 ================
Additional record documents reviewed for context:
8. Design Basis Memorandum, CB-DBM-001, Rev.2, Calloway Braddock, dated 11/14/2025 —
Section 7.3 (Shallow Foundations — Block C) and the geotechnical design parameters.
9. Sheet S-201, “Foundation Sections and Details,” Rev.4, Calloway Braddock, dated
05/29/2026 — Detail 3/S-201, Typical Spread Footing — Block C.
10. Sheet S-101, “Foundation Plan,” Rev.4, Calloway Braddock, dated 05/29/2026.
11. Boring Logs and Groundwater Monitoring Record, Appendix A to KGI-2024-0417 — Boring
B-09 (Block C centre).
12. Field Observation Report, Excavation and Groundwater, KGI-FO-2026-0528, Kelbrook
Geotechnical, Inc., dated 05/28/2026.


3. BASIS OF REVIEW
Governing tolerance. Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.6 (“Settlement Tolerance”)
establishes the controlling criteria: total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement 0.5
in maximum over 30 ft. Article 3.6 further provides that “where predicted or monitored
settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural Engineer of Record shall be
notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a written disposition is issued,”
and that cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance is to be reported immediately.
Design basis. Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001 Rev.2, Section 7.3, states that Block
C is founded on isolated spread footings bearing on the upper sand above the compressible CL
clay, that “settlement of the clay layer is a serviceability consideration and is checked in CB-
GEO-007,” and that settlement is checked under service-level combinations with tolerances
established in Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 (total 1.0 in, differential 0.5 in). The DBM lists the
governing clay parameters (H = 18 ft; γ = 120 pcf; Cc = 0.28; e0 = 0.92; σ’0 = 1,850 psf; σ’p
= 1,900 psf) and the Block C allowable bearing pressure of 4,000 psf net (at El. 748 ± 2 ft).
Geotechnical basis. GIR Rev.2, Executive Summary (recommendation 1) and Sections 8.1
and 9.1, assigns the consolidation-settlement computation to the Structural Engineer of
Record: the EOR “must explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress
increase q at mid-depth of the clay caused by each governing footing, using the parameters in
Table 5-1,” and “must reconcile [it] against the total-and-differential settlement tolerances.”
Section 8.1 gives the one-dimensional consolidation equation and Table 8-1 a sensitivity table
of Sc against q. Section 9.1 states that if computed settlement exceeds tolerance, “footing
sizes may be adjusted to reduce the stress increase, footings may be combined into a mat, or a
deep-foundation alternative may be considered.”
Parameters applied. The consolidation parameters are taken from Vantree report
VMT-2025-0109-CON (ASTM D2435, samples B-06 U3 and B-08 U2), as transcribed in GIR
Table 5-1 and CB-GEO-007 Sheet 5, and as recorded on the Register Reference Values tab: Cc
= 0.28; Cr = 0.045; e0 = 0.92; σ’0 = 1,850 psf (mid-clay, El. 729.0); σ’p = 1,900 psf (OCR
1.03, essentially normally consolidated); H = 18 ft (El. 738.0 to El. 720.0); double drainage; cv
≈ 0.042 ft²/day. The stress increase at mid-clay, Δσ = 900 psf, is as recorded in CB-GEO-007
(Sheet 2 and Sheet 5) and on the Register Reference Values tab.
Basis of review applied. I (a) confirmed whether CB-GEO-007 contains a complete long-term
(consolidation) settlement analysis; (b) independently computed the one-dimensional
consolidation settlement of the Stratum 2 clay using the GIR §8.1 equation and the recorded
parameters and Δσ; (c) compared the result to the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 tolerances; (d)
checked the founding geometry used in the calculation against the issued-for-construction
drawings; and (e) correlated the result with the Block C monitoring record and its trend.


4. FINDINGS
 ================ PAGE 3 ================
Finding 1 — The settlement calculation of record does not contain a long-term
(consolidation) analysis. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4, titled “Consolidation — Long-Term
Settlement Contribution — Stratum 2 CL Clay,” is left incomplete: every parameter cell carries
“—” and the sheet states “Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement
result on Sheet 3” (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 4).
The calculation’s serviceability conclusion rests solely on the immediate (elastic) settlement
computed on Sheet 3 by the Schmertmann strain-influence method — maximum total 0.9 in
(footing F-C6) and maximum differential 0.2 in — both reported within the 1.0 in / 0.5 in
tolerance (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 3, “Conclusion (Sheet 3)” and “Comparison to Tolerance”).
That computation is explicitly short-term: the time factor C2 is set to 1.00 with t = 0.1 yr, and
the Stratum 2 modulus used is a back-figured undrained Eu (≈ 150 tsf). It is an immediate-
settlement computation, not a long-term settlement computation (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 3,
correction factors and soil-modulus table).
Item 051 is expressly the long-term settlement of the clay. The DBM (§7.3) states that the clay
settlement is “checked in CB-GEO-007,” and the drawing note on Detail 3/S-201 states “Refer
to CB-GEO-007 for settlement calculation basis.” The long-term component is therefore
required but absent (DBM Rev.2, §7.3; Sheet S-201, Detail 3/S-201, Notes).
The settlement analysis in CB-GEO-007 is incomplete for the purpose of Item 051.
Finding 2 — The Geotechnical Investigation Report assigns the consolidation
computation to the EOR and supplies the method and a sensitivity table. GIR Rev.2
(Executive Summary, recommendation 1; §9.1) provides that Block C spread footings may be
founded in the upper sand, but requires that “the Structural Engineer of Record must explicitly
compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress increase q at mid-depth of the
clay caused by each governing footing, using the parameters in Table 5-1,” and that “the
computed settlement must be reconciled against the total-and-differential settlement
tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.”
GIR §8.1 states the one-dimensional consolidation equation, Sc = Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[(σ’0
+ q) / σ’0], and that for any q > (σ’p − σ’0) ≈ 50 psf, virgin (Cc) compression governs (GIR
Rev.2, §8.1).
GIR Table 8-1 tabulates the sensitivity of Sc to q at mid-clay: q = 100 psf → 0.7 in; 300 → 2.1
in; 600 → 3.8 in; 1,000 → 5.9 in; 1,200 → 6.8 in (GIR Rev.2, Table 8-1).
Finding 3 — Independent consolidation computation using the recorded Δσ = 900 psf
exceeds the total-settlement tolerance by a factor of about five. Working — applying the
GIR §8.1 equation with the recorded parameters (Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, H = 18 ft = 216 in, σ’0
= 1,850 psf) and the recorded stress increase at mid-clay Δσ = 900 psf (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 2
and Sheet 5; Register, Reference Values):
          Sc = [Cc · H / (1 + e0)] · log10[(σ’0 + Δσ) / σ’0]
            = [0.28 × 216 / (1 + 0.92)] · log10[(1,850 + 900) / 1,850]
            = [60.48 / 1.92] · log10[2,750 / 1,850]
            = 31.50 × log10[1.4865]
            = 31.50 × 0.17228
            ≈ 5.42 in.
A recompression/virgin split — Cr from σ’0 to σ’p, then Cc from σ’p to (σ’0 + Δσ) — gives Sc ≈
0.06 in + 5.06 in = 5.12 in, essentially the same result, because the OCR is only 1.03 and
nearly the full 900 psf increment lies on the virgin branch (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 5; GIR Table 5-
1).
The result is consistent with GIR Table 8-1: it falls between the q = 600 psf (3.8 in) and q =
1,000 psf (5.9 in) entries, as 900 psf does. I verified the Table 8-1 entries by recomputation (q
= 100 → 0.72 in; 300 → 2.06 in; 600 → 3.84 in; 1,000 → 5.91 in; 1,200 → 6.84 in).
 ================ PAGE 4 ================
Comparison to tolerance: Sc ≈ 5.42 in against the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 total limit of 1.0 in
is a utilisation of about 5.4×. Adding the immediate settlement (0.9 in, Schmertmann) gives a
long-term total of about 6.3 in, about 6× the tolerance. The long-term settlement exceeds the
total-settlement tolerance by a wide margin.
The result does not turn on the precise value of Δσ. Back-solving the GIR equation, the
consolidation settlement reaches 1.0 in at q ≈ 140 psf and 0.5 in at q ≈ 70 psf. Any realistic
spread-footing stress increase at this site produces a q at mid-clay well above 140 psf, so the
total-settlement tolerance is exceeded for any plausible footing-induced stress.
Finding 4 — The founding elevation used in CB-GEO-007 does not match the issued-
for-construction drawings and must be reconciled. CB-GEO-007, Sheet 2, takes the
underside of footing at El. 740.5, described as “isolated square spread footings on Stratum 1
sand, ~2.5 ft above top of clay” (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 2).
The issued drawings show the Block C typical spread footing with top of footing at El. 748.0
and underside at El. 746.0 (2’-0” thick), i.e., about 8 ft above the top of the Stratum 2 clay at
El. 738.0. The DBM states the 4,000 psf allowable bearing is applicable “at El. 748 ± 2 ft,”
consistent with the drawings (Sheet S-201, Detail 3/S-201; DBM Rev.2, geotechnical
parameters). Boring B-09 (Block C centre) logs the SP-SM upper sand from about El. 746.1 to
the clay contact at El. 738.0, confirming that the El. 746.0 founding lies within the upper sand
(Boring Logs, B-09).
The monitored column pedestals, at top elevations about El. 750.05, are consistent with a
roughly 2 ft pedestal on a footing topped at El. 748.0 (the drawing geometry), not with a
footing topped at about El. 743 (the calc geometry), corroborating the drawing founding
(Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 2 — Monitoring Points).
Consequence: the Δσ = 900 psf recorded in CB-GEO-007 was computed for a founding 5.5 ft
deeper (closer to the clay) than the issued drawings, and so over-states the stress at mid-clay
relative to the as-drawn/as-built geometry. A founding at El. 746.0 would reduce Δσ, and the
EOR must recompute Δσ at mid-clay for the as-drawn footing schedule (Sheet S-101) and
founding. This is a reconciliation item. It does not change Finding 3 in substance: even a
substantially reduced Δσ yields a consolidation settlement well above the 1.0 in tolerance (GIR
Table 8-1: q = 300 psf → 2.1 in; q = 600 psf → 3.8 in).
Finding 5 — The settlement monitoring is consistent with the early stage of a large,
slow consolidation and does not support closure against the tolerance. The latest
reading, 06/26/2026, is 0.61 in cumulative at MP-7 (interior footing FTG-C7, heaviest tributary
load), with the twelve points ranging from 0.31 in (MP-12) to 0.61 in (MP-7). All values are
within the 1.0 in total tolerance to date (Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 3 — Readings, Round
15; Sheet 1 — Observations Summary).
The trend has not stabilised. The round-to-round increment at MP-7 has risen from 0.03 in per
14 days (Rounds 2–4) to 0.07 in per 14 days (Round 14–15). The record states that “the
incremental settlement observed in the most recent three rounds … is equal to or greater than
the incremental settlement observed in the first three rounds” and “Rate not decreasing.” The
trend chart annotation records the curve as concave (downward) and that it “has not entered a
decelerating (concave-up) phase” (Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 1 — Observations Summary;
Sheet 4 — Trend Chart; Sheet 3 — Round-to-Round Increment at Worst Point).
The structure is still being loaded. The monitoring log records: footings and pedestals cast
12/2025; Level-1 columns and Level-2 slab framing 01–02/2026; Level-2 CMU partitions,
Level-3 framing and roof steel 03–05/2026; podium slab-on-grade placed 06/2026. Full service
(dead plus live) load is not yet applied (Settlement Monitoring, Sheet 5 — Notes).
Time-rate. With cv ≈ 0.042 ft²/day and double drainage (drainage path Hdr = 9 ft), primary
consolidation is slow: about 90% consolidation in roughly 1,635 days (≈ 4.5 years), consistent
with the GIR §8.1 statement that primary consolidation “require[s] on the order of several
years.” At 196 days of monitoring, the average degree of consolidation is on the order of one-
third, and less in practice because load is applied progressively (CB-GEO-007, Sheet 5; GIR
Rev.2, §8.1).
 ================ PAGE 5 ================
Correlation. The 0.61 in observed is small relative to the computed ≈ 5.4 in ultimate
consolidation and is consistent with a partially loaded structure in the early stage of a multi-
year consolidation. The accelerating, non-decaying trend is the expected signature of that
condition. The monitoring therefore corroborates, rather than refutes, the concern that the
long-term settlement will exceed the tolerance; it is not a basis on which Item 051 can be
closed against the tolerance.


5. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Determination. The Block C settlement analysis of record (CB-GEO-007) is not complete for
the purpose of Item 051: it computes the immediate (elastic) settlement only and omits the
long-term consolidation settlement of the Stratum 2 CL clay, which the GIR (§8.1, §9.1) and the
DBM (§7.3) require the EOR to compute and reconcile against the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6
tolerances. My independent computation of that long-term settlement, using the project’s own
recorded parameters and Δσ = 900 psf, gives Sc ≈ 5.4 in — about 5.4 times the 1.0 in total-
settlement tolerance (and about 6.3 in combined with the 0.9 in immediate settlement). The
result exceeds the total-settlement tolerance for any realistic stress increase at this site, and
the Block C monitoring (0.61 in, accelerating, non-decaying, structure not yet fully loaded,
multi-year consolidation) is consistent with the early stage of that settlement.
Disposition. NOT VERIFIED. Item 051 cannot be closed on the present record. I recommend
the register item be held Open, with the Thelbridge disposition recorded as NOT VERIFIED
(design review), pending the EOR action set out below.
Action required before the item can be closed.
1. The Structural Engineer of Record — Gregory Nash, PE, Calloway Braddock Structural
Engineers, LLC — must complete and reissue the Block C settlement calculation (CB-GEO-007,
Rev. X) to include the long-term one-dimensional consolidation settlement of the Stratum 2 CL
clay, computed per the GIR §8.1 equation with the Table 5-1 parameters, for the as-drawn/as-
built footing geometry. The reissue must in particular:
       a. Reconcile the founding elevation — the calculation is to use the issued-drawing
       founding (underside of footing El. 746.0 per Sheet S-201, Detail 3/S-201, within the
       DBM El. 748 ± 2 ft bearing band), not El. 740.5.
       b. Recompute the per-footing stress increase at mid-clay (El. 729.0) by
       Boussinesq/Newmark superposition for the as-drawn footing schedule (Sheet S-101)
       and founding.
       c. Compute the consolidation settlement (recompression plus virgin, recognising OCR
       1.03) for each governing footing and add the immediate (Schmertmann) settlement, to
       give the total long-term settlement.
       d. Compute the differential settlement between adjacent footings and check it against
       the 0.5 in-over-30 ft limit.
       e. Reconcile the result explicitly against Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 (1.0 in total / 0.5 in
       differential).
2. Because the predicted long-term settlement exceeds the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6
tolerance, the EOR must issue a written disposition of the Block C foundation scheme. The
remedies identified in GIR §9.1 are available to the EOR: enlarge or combine footings to
reduce the stress increase, convert to a mat foundation, or adopt a deep-foundation
alternative. The EOR’s written disposition is a required deliverable.
3. Until the EOR’s written disposition is issued, and in accordance with Spec 31 20 00 Article
3.6, no additional load is to be applied to the Block C foundations. I recommend that the
Owner’s Representative (Adrian Vance) notify the Structural Engineer of Record in writing of
the predicted exceedance, transmitting this verification, so that the Article 3.6 process is
formally initiated and the load restriction is placed on the record.
 ================ PAGE 6 ================
4. Block C settlement monitoring (Rowan Bay Constructors, Survey Crew 3 — D. Halloran,
PLS) is to continue at the established 14-day interval, or as the EOR directs following the
disposition, with readings transmitted to the Owner’s Representative; cumulative settlement
approaching either tolerance is to be reported immediately per Article 3.6. Monitoring is an
observation of performance; it is not, by itself, a closure deliverable for this item.

• Revised Block C settlement calculation (CB-GEO-007, Rev. X) including the long-term

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Generate the Item 051 verification memo from the Thelbridge template."""
import copy
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.text.paragraph import Paragraph

SRC = "/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_TEMPLATE_v1.docx"
OUT = "/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx"

doc = Document(SRC)
paras = doc.paragraphs

def clear_runs(p):
    for r in list(p.runs):
        r._element.getparent().remove(r._element)
    # also drop any stray hyperlink runs just in case
    for hl in p._p.findall(qn('w:hyperlink')):
        p._p.remove(hl)

def add_run(p, text, bold=False, italic=False, size=10.0, name='Calibri'):
    run = p.add_run(text)
    run.font.name = name
    run.font.size = Pt(size)
    run.bold = bold
    run.italic = italic
    return run

def set_header_field(p, label, value, size=10.0, tab_at=1.25):
    clear_runs(p)
    p.paragraph_format.tab_stops.add_tab_stop(Inches(tab_at))
    add_run(p, label, bold=True, italic=False, size=size)
    add_run(p, '\t', bold=False, italic=False, size=size)
    add_run(p, value, bold=False, italic=False, size=size)

def replace_body(p, segments, size=10.0, indent=None):
    """segments: list of (text, bold, italic)."""
    clear_runs(p)
    for (text, bold, italic) in segments:
        add_run(p, text, bold=bold, italic=italic, size=size)
    if indent is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    return p

def insert_after(ref_p, src_for_ppr, segments, size=10.0, indent=None):
    new_xml = copy.deepcopy(src_for_ppr._p)
    for r in new_xml.findall(qn('w:r')):
        new_xml.remove(r)
    for hl in new_xml.findall(qn('w:hyperlink')):
        new_xml.remove(hl)
    ref_p._p.addnext(new_xml)
    np = Paragraph(new_xml, ref_p._parent)
